text:
anya: Quick heads-up  found a small maintenance gap in the ruby SDK + sampleapp combo. When running behind some corporate proxies we see connection resets and sporadic 502s from the proxy.
michael: Any reproducible steps?
anya: Yes. Run sampleapp with heavy parallel requests (wrk) against local envoy with http/1.1 keep-alive enabled. After a few hundred reqs some requests get 502 and Net::ReadTimeout in app logs.
sophia: That's odd; ruby SDK uses Net::HTTP.start per request in HttpClient which should respawn sockets. Could it be socket reuse + proxy not liking keep-alive?
anya: Exactly. The SDK default uses a small thread-local persistent pool (to improve latency) and that interacts poorly with our local proxy that drops idle connections aggressively. On the Go/JS SDKs we open per-request connections by default so they didn't hit it.
michael: This is a parity + resilience issue. Options: 1) keep persistent pool but add aggressive health-check/reconnect, 2) change default to non-persistent for sampleapp quickstart, or 3) add an env flag to opt-out of persistent connections.
sam: I'm leaning to option 3 (feature flag) for now: add REDWOOD_DISABLE_CONN_POOL (or REDWOOD_CONN_MODE) so sampleapp/quickstart can opt-out, and keep optimized default for production users.\ophia: small nit: prefer a positive flag like REDWOOD_ENABLE_CONN_POOL=true, default true, and allow setting to false. Avoid negative config names.
michael: Agreed, use REDWOOD_ENABLE_CONN_POOL with default true. Sampleapp Quickstart sets it to false to avoid local proxy weirdness and our docs call out tradeoffs.
anya: I'll prototype a minimal change in HttpClient: if ENV['REDWOOD_ENABLE_CONN_POOL'] == 'false' then create a fresh Net::HTTP per request; else use existing pooled behavior. Also add a short integration test that runs against a mocked proxy that simulates connection-drop and asserts requests still succeed when pool disabled.
sophia: For the test, reuse tests/fixtures/local_proxy_stub so CI doesn't need real envoy. Make it deterministic.
michael: Important: add a short migration note in CHANGELOG about behavior change and how to opt-in. Also include a comment in code linking to the sampleapp issue.
sam: One more ask: please include a quick benchmark in the PR description comparing latency with pool enabled vs disabled for 1k concurrent calls. That helps reviewers understand perf tradeoffs.
anya: Will do. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-ruby/pull/812 (WIP) with patch and tests.
ci-bot: CI queued for PR 812: https://ci.redwood/sdk-ruby/812 :hourglass: 
ci-bot: CI failed on windows runner because the integration test spawns a UnixSocket (not supported on mingw). See logs: https://ci.redwood/sdk-ruby/812/logs/12
michael: We need the tests to be cross-platform. Wrap UnixSocket usage with a platform check and fallback to TCP loopback on Windows. Keep the same semantics.
sophia: Also add a small unit that fakes the proxy via TCP accept and send RST to simulate drop, so Windows/Mac/Linux can all run it.
anya: Updated tests to use TCP loopback when RUBY_PLATFORM =~ /mingw|mswin/ and UnixSocket otherwise. Pushed new commit.
ci-bot: CI queued again: https://ci.redwood/sdk-ruby/812 :hourglass: 
ci-bot: CI passed: https://ci.redwood/sdk-ruby/812 :white_check_mark: 
michael: Nice work. LGTM after one doc tweak: sampleapp quickstart should include a short note: "If you run behind a proxy that aggressively drops idle connections, set REDWOOD_ENABLE_CONN_POOL=false during local dev."
sam: Also add a line in devex FAQ: "Why do my local requests error with 502?" pointing to the env var and proxy header sizes/timeouts.
sophia: I'll merge and backport the change to the 1.x branch since support reported similar for on-prem customers.
anya: Thanks all. Will follow up with perf numbers in the PR thread and add the docs blurb. :thumbsup:
